stances_toward.note: No recognition (the dataset row says so) but unusually close ties built since Vystrcil's August 2020 visit: direct Taipei-Prague flights (2023), a CzechInvest office in Taipei (2024), a Czech Centre. Cooling because the Babiš cabinet refused a government aircraft for the Senate president's April 2026 trip; Hala's analysis calls the shift 'real, but shallow' and the institutional links intact. Bond - affinity: democratic kinship, Senate and Pavel's channel.

sources.title: Czech-Taiwan relations under Babiš: the shift is real, but shallow
Has Czechia's Taiwan policy lost its wings? Plane row signals new approach to China

stances_toward.note: Lithuania does not recognise Taiwan (a dataset row records that) but hosts the Taiwanese Representative Office, opened its own trade office in Taipei in Feb 2026, and trades EUR 191m (2025, from EUR 111m in 2021); Taiwanese direct investment rose from EUR 0.53m (2021) to EUR 7.21m (2024). Partner and not ally: this is transactional cooperation with no alignment, and Vilnius is now negotiating a normalisation that may cost the office its name. The president says Lithuania wants to balance the two. Bond - affinity: shared experience of a larger neighbour.
